Apple said today that a new UK proposal targeting App Store fees amounts to price regulation, warning it could harm innovation and investment. Details below.

Apple pushes back against UK App Store regulation proposal

According to Reuters, Apple today filed a formal response to the UK's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) consultation, opposing a proposed rule that would allow app developers to link to alternative payment methods.

The CMA has already designated both Apple and Google as having "strategic market status" in their respective mobile platforms, giving it the power to impose targeted requirements. Under the UK's new digital markets regime, this designation allows the regulator to introduce company-specific rules to promote competition and give consumers more choice.

Under the proposal, Apple and Google could still collect commissions on transactions completed via alternative payment methods, but any associated fees must be deemed "fair and reasonable."

Reuters noted that the CMA "expects guided fees to be lower than current app store charges, and believes the savings would benefit UK consumers or be reinvested by developers to support innovation."

Apple, however, takes a markedly different stance and has opposed the proposal. Reuters reports:

Same

The CMA has rejected Apple's characterisation of the proposal as price regulation, saying its purpose is to establish principles for determining whether guided fees are fair and reasonable, rather than to directly set fee levels.
